subject: biology

concepts.title: Reproductive Health and RCH Programmes
concepts.definition: A state of complete physical, mental, emotional, and social well-being concerning the reproductive system and its functions, supported by national initiatives like the both both both both both both both both both both both both Reproductive and Child Health Care (RCH) programmes.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Reproductive health extends beyond physical fitness to encompass both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both emotional and social aspects of human reproduction.
question_patterns: What does reproductive health mean according to WHO?
Explain the objectives of the Reproductive and Child Health Care (RCH) programmes.
What are the major tasks under the RCH programmes?
How does the society benefit from reproductive health awareness?

solution_steps.action: Define reproductive health according to WHO
solution_steps.explain: According to the World Health Organisation, reproductive health means total well-being in physical, emotional, behavioural, and social aspects of reproduction.

solution_steps.action: Detail the goals of RCH programmes
solution_steps.explain: The goals include creating awareness about reproduction-related aspects and providing facilities and support for building a reproductively healthy society.

concepts.title: Amniocentesis and its Regulation
concepts.definition: A prenatal diagnostic technique where amniotic fluid is analyzed to detect genetic abnormalities in the fetus, legally restricted to prevent its misuse for sex determination.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Amniocentesis is meant for detecting chromosomal disorders, but is legally banned for sex determination to prevent female foeticide.
question_patterns: Why is there a statutory ban on amniocentesis in India?
What is amniocentesis and how is it performed?
Which genetic disorders can be detected using amniocentesis?
Explain the misuse of amniocentesis.

solution_steps.explain: A small amount of amniotic fluid containing fetal cells is extracted from the uterus to analyze chromosomes and biochemical substances.
It is used to test for genetic disorders such as Down's syndrome, hemophilia, and sickle-cell anemia.

solution_steps.action: Explain the reason for the legal ban
solution_steps.explain: The test is banned for gender determination to legally check the increasing menace of female foeticide.

concepts.title: Natural Methods of Contraception
concepts.definition: Contraceptive practices that prevent fertilization by avoiding the meeting of sperm and ovum without using any artificial devices or chemicals.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Includes periodic abstinence (days 10-17), coitus interruptus, and lactational amenorrhea (up to 6 months post-partum).
question_patterns: Explain the natural methods of contraception.
What is lactational amenorrhea and what is its maximum duration of effectiveness?
How does periodic abstinence prevent conception?
What is coitus interruptus?

solution_steps.explain: The three methods are periodic abstinence, withdrawal (coitus interruptus), and lactational amenorrhea.

solution_steps.action: Explain the physiological basis of each method
solution_steps.explain: Periodic abstinence avoids coitus during the fertile period (days 10-17 of the cycle); withdrawal prevents insemination; lactational amenorrhea relies on the absence of ovulation during intense breastfeeding (up to 6 months).

concepts.title: Barrier Methods of Contraception
concepts.definition: Contraceptive methods that physically block sperm from reaching the ovum using mechanical barriers like condoms, diaphragms, cervical caps, or vaults.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Barriers prevent physical contact of gametes and, in the case of condoms, also protect against STIs and AIDS.
question_patterns: How do barrier methods prevent pregnancy?
Name some reusable female barrier contraceptives.
Why is the use of condoms highly recommended over other barriers?
What is the role of spermicidal creams used with barriers?

solution_steps.action: List the barrier devices for males and females
solution_steps.explain: Condoms are used by both males and females; diaphragms, cervical caps, and vaults are used by females.

solution_steps.action: Describe how they block sperm entry
solution_steps.explain: They cover the cervix or penis during coitus, physically blocking the entry of ejaculated semen into the female reproductive tract.

solution_steps.action: Highlight the dual benefit of condoms
solution_steps.explain: Condoms provide additional protection against contracting sexually transmitted infections (STIs) and AIDS.

concepts.title: Intrauterine Devices (IUDs)
concepts.definition: Devices inserted into the uterus by medical professionals that prevent conception by releasing copper ions, hormones, or acting as physical foreign bodies to suppress sperm both motility and implantation.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Categorized into non-medicated, copper-releasing, and hormone-releasing IUDs.
question_patterns: Classify the different types of Intrauterine Devices with examples.
How do copper-releasing IUDs prevent conception?
Explain the mechanism of hormone-releasing IUDs.
Why are IUDs widely accepted in India for spacing children?

solution_steps.explain: Non-medicated (e.g., Lippes loop), copper-releasing (e.g., CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375), and hormone-releasing (e.g., Progestasert, LNG-20).

solution_steps.action: Explain the mechanism of copper-releasing IUDs
solution_steps.explain: Released copper ions suppress sperm motility and their fertilizing capacity, while increasing phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus.

solution_steps.action: Explain the mechanism of hormone-releasing IUDs
solution_steps.explain: They make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and render the cervix hostile to the sperms.

concepts.title: Oral and Injectable Contraceptives
concepts.definition: In brief, Hormonal preparations containing progestogens or progestogen-estrogen combinations taken orally as pills or administered as injections/implants to inhibit ovulation and implantation.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Pills like 'Saheli' are non-steroidal and taken weekly, while others are indeed taken daily for 21 days.
question_patterns: How do oral contraceptive pills prevent pregnancy?
What is Saheli and why is it considered a major development in oral contraception?
Describe the administration pattern of daily oral pills.
What are implants and how do they differ from oral pills?

solution_steps.action: Describe the hormonal composition of pills and implants
solution_steps.explain: They contain small doses of either progestogens or progestogen-estrogen combinations.
They inhibit ovulation and implantation, and alter cervical mucus quality to prevent sperm entry.

solution_steps.action: Contrast daily pills with weekly non-steroidal pills like Saheli
solution_steps.explain: Saheli is a non-steroidal, once-a-week pill developed by CDRI, Lucknow, having high contraceptive value and minimal side effects.

concepts.title: Surgical Methods of Contraception
concepts.definition: Terminal contraceptive procedures that block gamete transport through surgical intervention, namely vasectomy in males and tubectomy in females.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, Highly effective but virtually irreversible methods of permanent contraception.
question_patterns: Distinguish between vasectomy and tubectomy.
Why are surgical methods of contraception considered terminal?
How does sterilisation prevent pregnancy without affecting gametogenesis?
What is the main drawback of surgical contraception?

solution_steps.explain: In vasectomy, a small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up. In tubectomy, a small part of the fallopian tube is removed or tied up.
These procedures block gamete transport, preventing sperm and ovum from meeting, while gamete production remains unaffected.
These techniques are highly effective but their reversibility is extremely poor.

concepts.title: Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP)
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, the intentional or voluntary termination of pregnancy before full term, regulated by strict legal provisions to prevent misuse.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, Safe during the first trimester (up to 12 weeks), and legalised in India since 1971 with amendments in 2017.
question_patterns: What is Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP)?
Under what conditions is MTP legalised in India?
Up to which week of pregnancy is MTP considered safe?
Explain the amendments made in the MTP Act in 2017.

solution_steps.explain: MTP is the voluntary or intentional termination of a pregnancy before it reaches full term.
MTPs are relatively safe during the first trimester (up to 12 weeks of pregnancy); second trimester abortions are much riskier.

solution_steps.action: Explain the legal conditions and grounds
solution_steps.explain: Legalised in 1971 to avoid misuse, and amended in 2017 to require opinions from registered medical practitioners based on risk to the mother's life or severe fetal abnormalities.

concepts.title: Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs)
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, Infections or diseases transmitted primarily through sexual contact, which can lead to severe complications if left untreated.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, Early detection is crucial; hepatitis-B, genital herpes, and HIV are currently incurable, while others are completely curable.
question_patterns: List some common sexually transmitted infections (STIs).
Which STIs are not completely curable?
What are the long-term complications of untreated STIs?
How can one prevent contracting sexually transmitted infections?

solution_steps.explain: Incurable STIs include hepatitis-B, genital herpes, and HIV. Others like gonorrhea, syphilis, and chlamydiasis are completely curable if detected early.

solution_steps.action: Describe early symptoms and long-term complications
solution_steps.explain: Early symptoms include itching, fluid discharge, and slight pain. Untreated STIs can lead to pelvic inflammatory diseases (PID), ectopic pregnancies, stillbirths, and infertility.
Prevention includes avoiding sex with multiple/unknown partners, using condoms during coitus, and seeking immediate medical attention in case of doubt.

concepts.title: Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART) - IVF, ZIFT, and IUT
concepts.definition: Special clinical procedures where fertilization is performed outside the body (in vitro) followed by transferring the embryo into the female reproductive tract.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: In brief, ZIFT involves transferring early embryos (up to 8 blastomeres) into the fallopian tube, while IUT involves transferring embryos with more than 8 blastomeres into the uterus.
question_patterns: Explain the test tube baby programme.
Differentiate between ZIFT and IUT.
What is In Vitro Fertilisation (IVF)?
When is embryo transfer (ET) recommended?

solution_steps.explain: In vitro fertilisation involves fusing ova and sperms outside the body under simulated laboratory conditions.
Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer involves transferring the zygote or early embryo (up to 8 blastomeres) into the fallopian tube.
Intra Uterine Transfer involves transferring embryos with more than 8 blastomeres directly into the uterus.

concepts.title: Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART) - GIFT, ICSI, and AI
concepts.definition: Specialized infertility treatments where gametes are directly manipulated or artificially introduced to achieve fertilization, either in vivo or in vitro.
concepts.formula: concept method; no single closed formula
concepts.key_idea: Includes GIFT (transfer of ovum), ICSI (direct injection of sperm), and AI/IUI (artificial introduction of semen).
question_patterns: What is GIFT and for whom is it recommended?
Explain Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI).
Under what conditions is Artificial Insemination (AI) used?
What is Intra-Uterine Insemination (IUI)?

solution_steps.explain: Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer involves transferring a donor's ovum into the fallopian tube of a female who cannot produce one but can support development.
Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection is a laboratory procedure where a single sperm is directly injected into an ovum to form an embryo.
Artificial Insemination involves introducing semen from a husband or donor artificially into the vagina or uterus (IUI) to correct low sperm count or inability to inseminate.

concepts.title: Estimation of Total Conceived Pregnancies
concepts.definition: In brief, a mathematical estimation of the total number of conceived pregnancies globally in a year using the number of performed Medical Terminations of Pregnancy (MTPs), given that MTPs account for a specific fraction (1/5th) of all conceptions.
concepts.key_idea: Since MTPs represent 20% (1/5th) of all conceived pregnancies, multiplying the annual MTP count by 5 yields the total annual conceptions.
question_patterns: If there are {mtps} million MTPs performed in a year, calculate the total number of conceived pregnancies.
How many total pregnancies are conceived annually if {mtps} million are terminated via MTP?
Find the total conceived pregnancies given that MTPs equal {mtps} million and represent one-fifth of all conceptions.
Calculate the total annual conceptions when the number of MTPs is {mtps}.

solution_steps.action: Identify the number of MTPs performed
solution_steps.explain: The given number of MTPs is stored in the variable mtps.
Multiply the MTP count by 5 to get the total conceived pregnancies.
